body:
pytest normally avoids `__main__.py` files not because of any specific `__main__.py` handling, but simply because the name `__main__.py` doesn't match the `test_*.py` or `*_test.py` patterns pytest looks for.

That said, `__main__.py` files are typically not considered modules, and even `multiprocessing` doesn't expect `__main__.py` files to have an `if __name__ == '__main__'` guard. Importing `__main__.py` is questionable behavior. Plus, `--doctest-modules` already avoids `setup.py`, which is a very similar case.
Closing this because it's been answered (and inactive for more than two weeks) :smile:
No, sorry, I should have read this more closely - I think you're right, and we should probably change this (though I haven't investigated in depth).

issue.title: #7124: Fix `--doctest-modules` crashing when `__main__.py` is present

issue.body:
Hi, hope you are all doing well.  Been a bit busy as of lately but I am hoping to start contributing again, here is an issue outlined in:

#7124

whereby when ``--doctest-modules`` was being passed, `ImportError` on `__main__.py` was raised, causing a crash.  I have added a special case for `__main__.py` here, similarly to `setup.py`, would welcome any feed back on this approach or if you can guide me to another one if this is incorrect.

 - adds `__main__.py` specific checks for the `doctest` plugin `collect_item` hook implementation
 - unit / integration tests
